stem:
Vivaan watches a Euglena under the school microscope. It swims, takes in food, and divides on its own in a single cell. He also studies one nerve cell on a chart of the human body and recalls that some microorganisms such as bacteria are unicellular.

Mark each statement true (T) or false (F).

statements.text: The Euglena is a complete living organism even though it has only one cell.
A single nerve cell taken from the human body chart is itself a complete living organism.
A bacterium is an incomplete living organism because it has only one cell.

teacher.key_rationale: Unicellular microorganisms such as Euglena and bacteria carry out all life functions in one cell, so they are complete organisms. A nerve cell is only one part of a multicellular body.
